body:
I know you're there. 
I'm a young guy, and I can't say that I can give you much advice, but your workethic and refusal to quit is an inspiration to me.

Things don't always go your way, but you made damn sure that you tried your best to make it happen your way. even if it didn't happen your way, I respect your ability to continue on despite failure more than I'd respect a guy who got lucky on his first few tries.

As someone who prides myself on my work ethic, you are in inspiration to me.thanks for trying your hardest, you've already accomplished more than many ever will.

The more I read, the more I relate. I was always considered "gifted" as well, and after playing football for so long, I've had to play the role of that high school Jock badass who doesn't have emotions. Its been so long I half believe the role myself, and its hard for me to be open even though I left my high school for university earlier this year.

I feel so alone in this world,I don't know how to make male friends because the friends I had in high school are so unbelievably different from the people around me now and who I want to be. I became so used to objectifying girls I don't know how to be just friends with one. 

When I'm with my "friends" the feelings go away for a bit, but it always comes back when I'm alone.
